question.leadin: Identify some people in the history of a certain empire that was neither holy nor Roman.
question.text: This Holy Roman Emperor, third of the Salian dynasty, was involved in the Investiture Controversy with the Papacy and stood in the snow for three days begging for forgiveness.
question.clue: This monarch defeated the first Percy rebellion at the Battle of Shrewsbury, which saw the death of Hotspur.

swap.text: The battles of Breteinfield and Lutzen took place during this major religious conflict, which lasted from 1618 to 1648.
swap.clue: This war's Bohemian phase ended at the Battle of White Mountain, which saw a victory for Count Tilly.

question.leadin: One monarch with this name legendarily raised several children without human interaction in an attempt to find a universal natural language.
question.text: Give this regnal name of the victor of the Sixth Crusade. An earlier Holy Roman Emperor with this name was defeated at Legnano [le-NYA-no] by the Lombard League.
question.clue: That king was buried in the Kyffhauser mountains and will rise in Germany's time of need, a legend transferred to his grandfather of the same name who lost the Battle of Legnano to the Lombard League.

swap.leadin: After this ruler won the 1159 Siege of Crema, he attempted to boss around the future pope Alexander III. Alexander's refusal led this man to support Victor IV in his bid to be pope.
swap.text: Name this Holy Roman Emperor that was excommunicated by Alexander III.
swap.clue: This man crossed the Saleph River to participate in a conflict he organized with Philip Augustus and Richard the Lionheart.

question.leadin: This Czech priest was burned at the stake for heresy in 1415 at the Council of Constance.
question.text: Name this man, who denounced the sale of indulgences by Antipope John XXIII. During a set of wars named for this man, handheld firearms such as hand cannons were first extensively used.
question.clue: This man's teachings were heavily influenced by those of John Wycliffe, although because of this he was convicted of heresy and burned at the stake at the Council of Constance.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about slave rebellions in the Western Hemisphere.
swap.text: A slave rebellion named after this holiday on the island of Jamaica was led by preacher Samuel Sharpe and mobilized up to 60,000 slaves in 1831. Also known as the Baptist War, this holiday also names an Australian island south of the island of Java.
swap.clue: British and German soldiers during World War I met in "no man's land" to celebrate this holiday.

question.leadin: Events in Eastern Europe sometimes happen in threes.
question.text: Though chronologically the third, the Second event of this name provoked the Thirty Years' War, when two Imperial governors were cast out of a window from the Bohemian Chancellery.
question.clue: The first, in 1419, involved the killing of seven council members by a crowd of Hussites.

swap.leadin: 27 leaders of one revolt named for this historic region were executed in the Old Town Square of its capital.
swap.text: Name this historic region in which Protestants revolted against Holy Roman Emperor Ferdinand II in 1618. That revolt began after two of the emperor's representatives were defenestrated in this historic region's capital.
swap.clue: A university in this region's New Town was founded by Charles IV, who was crowned after his blind father John died at the Battle of Crecy.

question.text: In its aftermath, Frederick fled to Breslau and attempted to negotiate with Ferdinand. For 15 points, Christian Anhalt was defeated by the Catholic League under Tilly in what battle that ended the Bohemian phase of the Thirty Years War?
question.clue: Descartes may have been present at this one-hour battle, as an observer in the army of the count of Bucquoy.

swap.text: In 1535, Suleiman lost Tunis to this Holy Roman Emperor, the son of Philip I and Joanna of Castille.
swap.clue: Long before his abdication to a monastery due to his gout, this ruler called Martin Luther to defend his views at the Diet of Worms ("vurms").

question.text: The 983 revolt was faced by the second emperor with this name. Margrave Gero, who campaigned against the Wends, served the first emperor with this name who was crowned by Pope John XII in 962.
question.answerHtml: Otto [accept Otto II or Otto I; accept Otto the Great]
question.clue: The fourth and final one was the only Welf to become emperor, but was defeated at the Battle of Bouvines, after which Frederick II restored the Hohenstaufen Dynasty.

swap.leadin: This ruler forgave his brother Henry of Bavaria for inciting rebellion with Eberhard of Franconia and Giselbert of Lotharingia.
swap.text: Name this son of Henry the Fowler who was crowned by Pope John XII in 962, becoming the first ruler of his namesake dynasty as well as the first ruler of the Holy Roman Empire.
swap.clue: Much of his ruling strength came from his namesake system of installing his own bishops, and later in his rule, he deposed John XII in favor of Leo VIII for the papacy.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the politics of the Holy Roman Empire.
question.text: A 1356 proclamation known by this name explicitly named the seven positions whose titles conferred elector status. A 1222 edict with this name ceded a number of rights to the Hungarian nobility.
question.answerHtml: Golden Bull [or Golden Bull of 1356; or Golden Bull of 1222; or chrysobull; prompt on “bull”]
question.clue: Emperor Frederic II was identified as the source of the 1218 one of Berne, considered a forgery, but definitely did issue one dealing with the holdings of Teutonic knights in Prussia named for the town of Rimini.

swap.leadin: As a result of declarations made at this event, Jacob Poost was arrested, while Jan van Essen and Hendrik Vos were burnt at the stake.
swap.text: Name this event condemning a man who defended his views from Leo X's ("the tenthʼs") bull Exsurge domine. Johann Eck presided over this event, during which its central participant may have said "Here I stand, I cannot do otherwise."
swap.clue: One prominent participant in this meeting had to hide at the Wartburg at its conclusion.

question.text: This league defeated at the Battle of Muhlberg was a militarized version of the earlier League of Torgau and was composed of Lutheran German princes who opposed Charles V.
question.clue: Taking its name from a town in Thuringia, this group was first formed by Philip I of Hesse and John Frederick I of Saxony.

swap.leadin: This emperor besieged Viterbo to restore a loyal imperial garrison, only to see papal representative Ranieri Capocci ("ron-YAIR-ee ka-PO-chee") massacre the loyalists after he signed a peace treaty.
swap.text: Name this emperor who promulgated the Constitutions of Melfi in his Kingdom of Sicily. This husband of Yolande of Jerusalem launched the Sixth Crusade to recapture the holy city.
swap.clue: This 13th-century king, called Stupor Mundi or "the astonishment of the world," drew on an Arabic text by Moamin to write "On the Art of Hunting With Birds" in his Sicilian court.

question.text: When the undefeated John Zizka was replaced by Procopius the Great as leader of the Taborite army, emperor Sigismund and the utraquists teamed up to smack him down in this 1434 battle also known as Cesky Brod.
question.clue: The Taborites were eventually defeated by an Utraquist coalition at this battle, after which they made peace with the Council of Basel via the Compact of Iglau.

swap.text: This one-eyed general revolutionized mobile warfare by mounting cannons on armored wagons and led the Taborites to a series of victories over the Bohemian Crusade. After his 1424 death, Taborite leadership passed to Procop the Great.
swap.clue: This one-eyed Taborite general, a reformist commander in the Hussite Wars, withstood Sigismund's siege of Prague at the Battle of Vitkov Hill. His tactics included arming wagon circles with cannons.

question.text: Frederick Barbarossa withdrew his support of Antipope Callixtus III after this 1176 battle, in which he was decisively defeated by Alberto da Guissano and the forces of the Lombard League.
question.clue: The carroccio, an oxen-drawn war wagon topped with a sacred altar, was used at this 1176 battle, which prompted its loser to sign the Treaty of Venice.

swap.leadin: John George of Saxony was one of the electors who opposed it. FTPE.
swap.text: Identify this 1629 decree, in which Holy Roman Emperor Ferdinand II called for secularized bishoprics, such as Bremen, to be placed back under the control of the Catholic Church.
swap.clue: Maximilian von Trautmannsdorf's Points of Pirna attempted to reconcile one party who had been alienated by this declaration, which was defended vociferously in Paul Laymann's Pacis Composito.
